text:
maria: heads-up — prototyping a new synthetic traffic generator called 'burst-critic' to exercise kernel selection + kv-cache warmup + long-tail latency. want quick feedback on metrics/output shape before i wire it into the replay harness.
lee: nice. what's different from the existing surge/weave generators?
aj: high level: three pieces — (1) microburst clusters with variable intra-burst qps, (2) long inter-burst tails (pareto-ish) to hit p999, (3) deterministic kv-cache warmup patterns so we can compare apples-to-apples across kernel variants.
sri: love the deterministic kv warmup — can you make the seed + prefix sequences replayable to the dev harness? we need exact request ids so kernel-switch accounting matches.
maria: yes, plan is to emit two artifacts per run: a compact replay log (req id, model, seqlen, kv-ops) + a seed file. will put on s3://redwood-bench/burst-critic/{run_ts}/.
natalie: outline of metrics we should capture: p50/p95/p99/p999 latency, tail-qps, batch-size histogram, kernel-selection counts, kv-cache hit/miss per step, kv-cache footprint over time, compile-time events, fallback events. also collect per-token cost estimate.
ben: add 'batching latency penalty' — time waiting to form batch. that's important for throughput vs latency tradeoffs.
maria: agreed. draft config snippet below (proto):
```yaml
name: burst-critic
seed: 3246789012
phases:
  - name: warmup
    qps: 10
    duration_s: 60
    kv_warmup: prefix-repeat
  - name: microburst
    pattern: clustered
    bursts: 120
    burst_qps: {min: 200, max: 1200}
    burst_duration_ms: {min: 50, max: 800}
  - name: longtail
    distribution: pareto
    alpha: 1.6
    duration_s: 300
replay_artifact: true
metrics: [latency_histogram, batch_histogram, kernel_switch_counts, kv_hit_rate]
```
lee: nice config. two thoughts: (A) ensure we can force 'kv-cold' reads mid-burst to observe parity between kernels; (B) expose a 'sticky-model' flag so runtime can't auto-fallback mid-run when testing a single kernel variant.
sri: for apples-to-apples we should run the same replay artifact across kernels, pinned model version, and same hardware. also fix sequence-length distribution. any runtime fallback should be a separate experiment.
junior note (maria): i'll add a 'forced-cold-at' schedule point where a downstream cache invalidation event clears selected shards.
perf-ci-bot: benchmark-run queued: burst-critic seed=3246789012 config=warmup+microburst+longtail. tracking id bc-3246.
aj: how are we going to interpret kernel-switch counts? suggest normalizing by total tokens served and by active sequences during switch. we want per-switch latency delta.
maria: we'll export a small CSV: (timestamp, kernel_from, kernel_to, active_sequences, delta_p50_ms, delta_p99_ms). then we can correlate with batch-size histogram.
ben: another important signal: 'kv-warmth curve' — fraction of requests that hit filled kv per time window. helps explain long-tail spikes.
natalie: also collect traces (sampled), with KV op annotations, kernel id, and batch composition. 1 trace per 10k requests should be fine.
lee: sanity check: we should run three experiment modes: smoke (1 run), compare (run N kernels sequentially on same artifact), and soak (24h continuous with periodic cold events).
maria: yep. plan: smoke -> local dev; compare -> dedicated infra on same instance type; soak -> dedicated cluster with autoscale toggled off. schedule next week for compare.
sri: don't forget to pin compiler flags / cuda driver versions. those change perf subtly. add them to run metadata.
maria: will do. also adding a small regression detector: after each compare run the perf pipeline computes p99 delta and flags >5% regression. perf-ci-bot should post results.
perf-ci-bot: bc-3246 compare complete. results: kernel-a vs kernel-b on same artifact: p99 delta +8.3% (regression), batch-median changed from 12 -> 8, kv_hit_rate unchanged. see s3://redwood-bench/bc-3246/results.json
lee: ^ that's actionable. smaller batches could explain higher p99. does kernel-b change batching heuristics? maybe kernel selection caused more singletons.
aj: I'll run a profiling capture for kernel-b with batch-size breakdown and KV op timings. expect to see higher per-token kernel overhead when batch<10.
ben: when you do profiling, please include wall-clock timeline + CPU/GPU utilization so we can see scheduling pauses.
maria: thanks. action items: (1) aj run profile for kernel-b and link traces, (2) lee confirm forced-cold schedule implementation, (3) natalie add regression threshold/alerts to perf pipeline, (4) ben add kv-warmth visual to dashboard, (5) i'll publish replay artifact and kick off compare runs.
ops-bot: scheduled job bc-3246-compare started on infra-red-12 at 3246789620
sri: small note — for reproducibility store the exact docker image sha and kernel module versions in run metadata.
maria: noted. i'll post the run artifact later today. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
lee: if kernel-b is consistently worse in p99 we should also test quantized variants — sometimes quantization interacts with batch packing in weird ways.
aj: yep. i'll add a quick variant sweep to the compare pipeline (q4_0, q4_1, fp16) but keep it optional.
maria: okay closing thread for now, will ping when results + traces are uploaded.
